S1.why: Numeral plus partitive, the way a Finnish label counts; 'ilmainen' is the everyday word for free and is used in every key.

S2.why: A short sinä imperative reads as an invitation in Finnish UI; 'Tilaa' was avoided everywhere because it is also the verb 'subscribe'.

S3.s: Olet käyttänyt kaikki %lld ilmaista cutlingiasi. Ne pysyvät ilmaisina ja toimivat edelleen.
S3.back: You-have used all 5 free cutlings-your. They stay free-as and work still.
S3.why: Item word lowercased mid-sentence as the vocab file does; possessive suffix -si keeps it personal; 88 characters.

S4.why: States the fact rather than 'you can'; 'ensimmäiset' also tells that these first ones stay free.

S5.why: 3/5 is read aloud 'kolme viidestä', so the noun takes elative singular to agree; positional placeholders.

S6.why: Nominative headline; partitive 'Tilaa' would read first as the imperative 'Subscribe', which S11 promises there is none of.

S7.s: Voit tallentaa jopa %@ teksticutlingia ja %lld kuvacutlingia.
S7.back: You-can save up-to 5,000 text-cutlings and 500 image-cutlings.
S7.why: Uses the vocab's own compound names Teksticutling and Kuvacutling so text and image items keep their one name; 'jopa' for up to, 'enintään' sounds like a limit.

S8.why: Finnish lists join the last item with 'ja' and no comma before it.

S9.s: Yksi osto riittää kaikille Apple-tiliisi kirjautuneille laitteille.
S9.back: One purchase suffices for-all Apple-account-your signed-in devices.
S9.why: Echoes the vocab sentence 'Apple-tiliisi kirjautuneilla laitteilla' so the account and devices are named as the app already names them; 67 characters.

S10.why: Second person present, plain and warm; 'osto' and 'maksaa' are the only money words used across the set.

S11.s: Ei tilausta, ei mainoksia, ei rekisteröitymistä.
S11.back: No subscription, no advertisements, no registering.
S11.why: The standard Finnish three-part negation for this promise; 'rekisteröityminen' is the usual word for signing up.

S12.why: The wording Finnish iOS apps use for the App Store restore action (ChatGPT's Finnish settings: Asetukset, Tili, Palauta ostot); fixes 'osto' as the one word for purchase.

S13.why: Impersonal passive present, how Finnish UI shows work under way; single ellipsis character.

S14.why: 'Avaa lukitus' is the Finnish unlock; 'hintaan' carries the price without putting a case ending on 4,99 €; 21 characters plus the price.

S16.why: The polite Finnish putting-off phrase; 'Ei nyt' sounds like a refusal.

S17.why: The verb iOS uses on Finnish close buttons.

S18.why: Warm and a little proud, and 'kaikki' includes the room the grid shows; 19 characters.

S19.s: Kiitos ostostasi. Se tukee Cutlingia ja sen ainoaa tekijää.
S19.back: Thanks for-purchase-your. It supports Cutling and its only maker.
S19.why: Keeps 'osto' (elative + -si); 'ainoa tekijä' says one person makes it without English 'indie developer' phrasing; app name inflected as Finnish does names.

S20.s: Tervetuloa takaisin. Aiempi ostosi on palautettu.
S20.back: Welcome back. Earlier purchase-your is restored.
S20.why: 'palautettu' ties the greeting to the Palauta ostot link the person just tapped.

S21.why: Numbers stand in nominative so VoiceOver never has to inflect a digit and the form holds for 1; total first, as a Finn would say it, so placeholders are positional.

S22.why: Label-and-number form works for 1, 2, 5 and 21 without plural forms; 'mahtuu' keeps 5,000 in nominative for speech.

S23.s: Cutlingin lukitus on avattu. Siihen mahtuu nyt %@ cutlingia.
S23.back: Cutling's lock is opened. Into-it fits now 5,000 cutlings.
S23.why: Genitive 'Cutlingin lukitus' is the natural unlocked announcement; numeral plus partitive is correct for 5,000.

S24.why: Calm, names what happened, blames no one; 18 characters.

S25.s: App Storeen ei saada juuri nyt yhteyttä. Yritä hetken kuluttua uudelleen.
S25.back: To-App-Store not get right now connection. Try in-a-moment's time again.
S25.why: Impersonal 'ei saada yhteyttä' is the idiomatic no-connection phrasing; 73 characters.

S26.s: App Store ei vahvistanut tätä ostoa.
S26.back: App Store did-not confirm this purchase.

S27.s: Tämän laitteen Apple-tilillä ei ole aiempaa Cutling-ostoa.
S27.back: This device's Apple-account-on is-not earlier Cutling-purchase.
S27.why: 'Cutling-osto' hyphenates the name in a compound as Finnish requires; 58 characters.

S28.s: Ilmaisversioon mahtuu %lld cutlingia. Avaa Cutlingin lukitus kerran, niin voit tallentaa vapaasti.
S28.back: Into-free-version fits 5 cutlings. Open Cutling's lock once, so you-can save freely.
S28.why: 'Ilmaisversio' is the usual Finnish name for a free version; the 'avaa…, niin…' pattern is how a Finn gives a condition aloud; 95 characters.

S29.why: Label then value, as a grey subtitle reads; 21 characters, 3 over the 18 budget, because every shorter form dropped either 'free' or 'used'.

K1.why: Definite 'Ilmaiset 5' means all of them without an extra word; ends on the action the tap takes, no full stop on it; 36 characters.

M1.why: Verb-led command name as Finnish Mac window titles are; 22 characters.

M2.why: Same command as M1 with the ellipsis character because it opens a window.

M3.why: Row label in nominative plural; item word lowercased after the first word as in the vocab sentence.

M4.why: Compact number pair, no words needed next to the M3 label.

M5.why: The status phrase Finns know from their own phones; 'Cutling avattu' would read as 'Cutling opened'.

M6.s: Yksi osto avaa Cutlingin lukituksen iPhonessa, iPadissa ja Macissa.
M6.back: One purchase opens Cutling's lock on-iPhone, on-iPad and on-Mac.
M6.why: Device names take the inessive -ssa/-ssä as Apple's Finnish does; 67 characters.

M7.s: Lukitus avattu iPhonessa, iPadissa ja Macissa tällä Apple-tilillä.
M7.back: Lock opened on-iPhone, on-iPad and on-Mac with-this Apple-account.
M7.why: Repeats the M5 status words so the row and the line under it agree; 66 characters.

M8.s: Ostit Cutlingin ennen kuin siitä tuli ilmainen, joten lukitus on avattu pysyvästi. Kiitos tuestasi.
M8.back: You-bought Cutling before it became free, so lock is opened permanently. Thanks for-support-your.
M8.why: 'siitä tuli ilmainen' is how Finns say an app went free; thanks for support, not for the purchase, since the payment was long ago; 99 characters.
